blacklistabilityReview.evidence: All four live implementations authorize chain-local Safe 0xf25c404c101d40d88b5dcd64b82583dbc918dd25 for forceTransfer(address,address,uint256) and arbitrary-holder burn(address,uint256), while the shared mint EOA lacks those permissions. Nonzero seizure simulations against actual holders succeeded on Ethereum block 25590408 (hash 0x114ec56a77156d27c6d2d91bf401ca428ffed4aa85f0ff0371b34af67f109052), Base block 48979919 (hash 0x4e8d1eed9b32347b239c53b681c713a167c3f491f0af1b79b7072d0ba3732c83), and Arbitrum block 486632328 (hash 0xc536c0320873e43c1c1d63ee1fdc6cd1b63ccf61cf61ac7c54867bfda503faeb); Monad block 89486097 (hash 0x6d816fae89965dc2323f02e29116adb6550c83b4a8870f8f75d539d10cf1b0be) confirmed selector authorization and a successful Safe call. Current Safe thresholds are Ethereum 3-of-8, Base 3-of-7, Arbitrum 4-of-8, and Monad 4-of-8.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Multipli issues rwaUSDi natively on Ethereum, Base, Monad, and Arbitrum; the four reviewed routes remain issuer-native. The latest implementation is CCIP-admin/IBurnMintERC20-compatible, but official Chainlink Token Manager/CCIP Directory lookups for the exact token addresses returned no configured-network row in this review, and no TokenPool, remote token, or active lane was verified. The unresolved CCIP binding is bridge-evidence follow-up in Bridge Risk; it does not make the four authored deployments representations. Ethereum in the peripheral route rows is an identity/accounting convention, not evidence that Base, Monad, or Arbitrum are bridged.
